title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Valencia Health
topics: Regional data residency and egress constraints
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a POC scoping call with Valencia Health to align on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), strict data residency needs for EU-only patient data, egress constraints, and concrete POC success criteria. Customer wants a 4-week pilot with benchmarks: 200ms median per-request latency for chat generation, 5k qps inference bursts testing, and proof that all PHI never leaves EU networks. Agreed next steps include diagrams, security docs, and a short benchmark plan to run in customer VPC or via PrivateLink.
next_steps: Evan to share Private Networking guide + network diagram (VPC peering and PrivateLink options) by 2027-11-02
Priya to propose benchmark plan (traffic profile, test prompts, tooling) by 2027-11-04
Valencia to confirm target region(s) and regulatory boundary (EU-only or specific countries) by 2027-11-01
Schedule technical runbook call with Valencia infra and security (1 hour) week of 2027-11-08
action_items: Evan: send network diagram + high-level POC SOW - due 2027-11-02
Priya: baseline benchmark script and expected metrics (p99, median, tokens/sec) - due 2027-11-04
Valencia (Mark): provide VPC CIDRs and peering constraints - due 2027-11-01
Allison: list of compliance controls (data residency, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS) to validate - due 2027-11-03
transcript: 15:00:00 Evan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick check audio?
15:00:05 Lena (Valencia CTO): sounds good, thanks Evan. we have about 40 minutes, agenda is to scope the POC networking and residency stuff
15:00:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Great, i'll run through networking options and then we can map success criteria and benchmarks
15:00:20 Mark (Infra): quick background — we're a healthcare SaaS with EU patient data, we need to guarantee data doesn't egress outside EU for certain workloads
15:00:30 Allison (Security): and we have SOC2 plus local country regs, so network isolation and audit logs are must-haves
15:00:40 Evan: Understood. two main ways customers connect to Redwood Private: VPC peering (private routing) or AWS PrivateLink endpoints. each has tradeoffs, we'll cover them
15:01:05 Priya: VPC peering gives you direct routing between your VPC and a Redwood VPC; L3 route based, good throughput and low latency, but requires route table management and inter-account peering

15:01:30 Priya: PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoints) is more controlled — you get an ENI per AZ, simpler security posture — traffic stays on AWS backbone and you can avoid cross-account route table exposure
15:01:50 Mark: latency wise any difference? for our real-time clinician chat we need sub 200ms median ideally, p99 < 500ms

15:02:05 Priya: In our experience, VPC peering slightly lower latency at same region because it's direct. PrivateLink can add a few ms but is more firewall-friendly. the bigger factor is where the inference nodes run — same AZ vs cross-AZ vs cross-region

15:02:30 Evan: Important note on data residency: Redwood can operate in region-specific deployments — we can pin model serving to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 and ensure logs and payloads don't leave region for designated workloads
15:02:45 Lena: That matters. We need proof during the POC that PHI never leaves EU. Can Redwood run entirely in our chosen region and show audit logs?
15:03:00 Oliver (CSM): Yes, we can enable region pinning and provide request-level audit logs. we'll also sign into the SOW that the POC uses EU-only endpoints
15:03:15 Allison: Also KMS — keys must be under our control, or at least in our KMS in the same region. how do you handle that?
15:03:28 Priya: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) in Private mode. for POC we can demonstrate encryption in transit and at rest with your KMS in eu-west-1
15:03:45 Ravi (DevOps): Network egress costs are a concern. If we peer, will there be data transfer charges?

15:03:55 Evan: For VPC peering within same region typically there are no cross-AZ charges from Redwood side; egress depends on cloud provider policy. with PrivateLink you pay for interface endpoints. we can model costs in the POC based on your expected token volumes

15:04:20 Priya: Let's talk success criteria. typical POC asks we propose: 1) functional connectivity without public internet, 2) region-locality verification (logs show EU-only), 3) performance benchmarks e.g., median latency <200ms for standard chat prompt, p99 <500ms for 95% of traffic, 4) throughput target — sustained 200 requests/sec with bursts to 1k/sec for short windows, 5) correctness/quality baseline against your prompt set
15:04:55 Lena: That matches what we need. For throughput, our peak is around 300 rps for message generation during morning triage, but we'd like headroom to 1k bursts
15:05:08 Priya: ok will size tests around 300 sustained with 1k burst. what about token sizes? average response ~150 tokens, some long notes 800 tokens

15:05:18 Mark: average 150 sounds right; we do have a small percentage of long generation for discharge summaries ~800 tokens. we want KV cache behavior to avoid re-encoding prompts when continuing context
15:05:35 Priya: noted — we'll include tests for long-context runs and streaming behavior. we'll also check kv-cache reuse across requests if you pin sessions
15:05:50 Allison: Compliance wise we need audit trail showing which model version served the request, timestamp, source IP (internal), and that the data stored for caching is encrypted
15:06:05 Evan: We'll include model-version tagging in logs and provide sample log export. Redwood can also mask or redact tokens in logs per your policy
15:06:20 Ravi: For the POC environment — can we host agents in our VPC or does Redwood need to host everything?

15:06:30 Priya: Two options: 1) Private deployment where Redwood runtime components are deployed in your VPC (we can do a customer-managed deployment), or 2) hosted Redwood with PrivateLink/VPC peering so traffic stays on the cloud backbone and data stays in-region. For POC we often do option 2 with PrivateLink because it's faster to stand up
15:06:55 Lena: Time is tight — 4 weeks is our target to evaluate. Is that realistic?

15:07:02 Evan: Yes 4 weeks is common. Week 1: network setup and connectivity validation, week 2: baseline benchmarks and model selection, week 3: tuning (batching, quant profiles), week 4: final run and deliverables
15:07:18 Priya: We'll provide a benchmark plan doc with scripts and expected metrics. you'll run tests from your VPC endpoints or we can orchestrate load from a controlled test harness — preference?
15:07:30 Mark: Prefer tests from our VPC to measure real path. we'll share ephemeral test nodes
15:07:40 Priya: Perfect. for PrivateLink we'll need your account ID and desired endpoint subnets so we can provision interface endpoints; for peering we'll need CIDR ranges and route permissions
15:07:55 Evan: Document wise I'll send our networking guide with diagrams showing both topologies — we'll call out security groups, route table adjustments, and sample NACLs
15:08:06 Allison: Also need to see a short security questionnaire / SOC2 artifacts before we start
15:08:12 Oliver: We'll attach our security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary) and a redacted architecture diagram for the POC
15:08:25 Ravi: About metrics — can you capture per-token cost metrics, token/sec, and per-route latency so we can estimate monthly costs?
15:08:33 Evan: Yes Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards and cost estimates. For POC we'll give a sample cost calculator
15:08:45 Priya: On the benchmarking: we'll run three profiles: low-latency chat (150 tokens), long-context generation (800 tokens), and high-throughput embedding/rerank sample if you use embeddings
15:09:00 Lena: We mostly need chat and long docs. embeddings are lower priority for now
15:09:10 Priya: Ok will focus on chat & long generation. For long context we may recommend a quantization profile to keep latency acceptable; we'll test both fp16 and int8-like variants
15:09:25 Mark: About regionality — we have two EU VPCs (eu-west-1 and eu-central-1) for redundancy. we'd like to ensure both remain EU-only and avoid cross-border egress to us-east-1 during failover

15:09:40 Evan: We can set regional routing policies so requests from eu-central go to eu-central servers. failover to another EU region is possible but we'll ensure we don't route outside EU. if you want cross-region failover to US, that will be a different policy and flagged
15:09:55 Allison: And during the POC we need a signed commitment that test traffic flagged as PHI will remain eu-resident and logs show that — even if a node failsover occurs
15:10:10 Oliver: We'll include that in the POC SOW: regional pinning for flagged datasets and a short runbook for failover behavior
15:10:22 Priya: For benchmarks we'll capture median, p95, p99, tokens/sec, and success rate. We'll also capture cold-start behavior for model spin-ups if you use burst mode
15:10:35 Ravi: Cold start is a big concern — some models take several seconds to spin up. do you have a warm pool option?
15:10:44 Evan: Redwood Dedicated supports warm pools and prewarmed model instances; for hosted we can reserve capacity or use fast start model variants. we'll show tradeoffs in the plan
15:10:58 Lena: Ok timeline recap: we need diagrams + security pack by next week, benchmark plan early the week after, and infra inputs (CIDRs, account IDs) from us asap
15:11:10 Evan: Yep. we'll send the network guide and SOW template today. Priya will send benchmark scripts by Thursday. schedule technical runbook for week of Nov 8
15:11:25 Mark: One more question — if we go PrivateLink and you push kernel updates / runtime changes, how are those coordinated?
15:11:35 Priya: For Private mode we have an upgrade window; we coordinate with your infra, can do staged canaries. we log version changes in the console and in API responses
15:11:50 Allison: And retention — how long do you store request logs for the POC? we want minimal retention and ability to purge
15:11:58 Evan: We'll set retention to 7 days for POC logs unless you request otherwise, and we support on-demand deletion of logs tied to specific request IDs
15:12:10 Ravi: any blockers for us to start networking this week?

15:12:15 Priya: We just need the account ID and target subnets for PrivateLink, or CIDR ranges and peering permissions for peering. Once we have that, we can provision the endpoints in 1-2 business days
15:12:30 Lena: We'll aim to get that to you by Monday. final question: will you help with a short cost estimate for our expected 100k tokens/day average?
15:12:40 Evan: Yes we'll model costs in the POC package. Priya — anything else to capture?

15:12:45 Priya: I'll include tests for streaming, KV-cache reuse, and a stress test for burst to 1k rps. Also include a small checklist to validate that traffic never crosses out of EU during the test
15:13:00 Oliver: i'll follow up with the security pack and SOC2 artifacts. worth noting some transcriptions sometimes have minor label errors, so we'll attach raw logs and a short meet recap email
15:13:10 Lena: Great, thanks everyone. that's helpful. we'll review the SOW and get infra details to you
15:13:18 Evan: thanks all — we'll send the docs and SOW today. talk soon
15:13:25 (call ends)
